name: SIGINT
standfirst: Security research and practitioner news, scored for novelty and actionability.
colophon: sigint.wtf — the correct response to most of these CVEs. Scored by machine against a hand-written rubric; ranking is opinion, not fact.

items.title: CVE-2025-68686 — Fortinet FortiOS Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor Vulnerability
items.dek: Fortinet FortiOS. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 10 August.

items.title: CVE-2026-16812 — Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator On-Prem OS Command Injection Vulnerability
items.dek: Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 30 July.

items.title: Are You Still the Agent I Authorized? Earned Authority under a Fixed Ceiling for Evolving Agents
items.dek: Formalizes authorization continuity for evolving agents: when tool grants remain valid after a model acquires skills or changes behavior, fixed ceiling and envelope model.
items.unproven: whether state-bound model integrates with existing tool-policy frameworks or requires separate governance layer; no reference implementation

items.title: Isolated but Exposed: Persistence-Based Memory Extraction Attack on LLM Agents
items.dek: Tool interface enables memory exfiltration from isolated LLM agent storage, bypassing user-level isolation.
items.unproven: Validated only on constructed agents; does not cover LLM providers' deployed production mitigations or tool-call rate-limiting in live systems.

items.title: The Illusion of Secure LLM Code: Closing the Security Gap via Iterative Reprompting
items.dek: Five LLM code assistants fail to generate NIST-compliant authentication code without iterative reprompting; single-shot NIST context alone insufficient.
items.unproven: whether iterative reprompting generalizes to other security domains or remains limited to authentication; tested on five models and one task class

items.title: Do LLMs Know Their Vulnerable Scenarios?
items.dek: Mechanistic interpretability links scenario-wrapped jailbreaks to internal scenario directions; Concept2Scenario framework identifies vulnerable scenario combinations.
items.unproven: generalization to models beyond three tested; whether identified scenarios enable hardening or only explain existing failures

items.title: False Prophets: On the Security of World Models in Agentic Systems
items.dek: Agents using world models can be manipulated to execute malicious code with 95% success rate via misprediction attacks on environment simulators.
items.unproven: whether defenses proposed hold against adaptive attackers; effectiveness in production agent deployment; cost of proposed mitigations

items.title: Exploiting Volvo/Eicher's fleet platform to gain control over all users/vehicles
items.dek: Authentication bypass in Volvo/Eicher fleet management platform permits unauthorized control of connected vehicles across user accounts.
items.unproven: Whether vulnerability affects production deployments or only test instances; no public PoC or active exploitation evidence provided; remediation timeline unknown.

items.title: ZKP Security Tools and Verification: Coverage, Effectiveness, Adoption, and Challenges
items.dek: Survey of ZKP bug-detection tools finds 45.7% detection on isolated code, 19.6% on full codebases, with Circom dominance and newer DSLs underserved.
items.unproven: effectiveness across production ZKP codebases and whether tool improvements would close the gap or hit fundamental limits

items.title: Poster: Rethinking Security in LLM Code Generation through Real-World Risk Scenarios
items.dek: LLMs generate code with over 56% vulnerability rates under realistic conditions including ambiguous requirements, under-specified context, and security-functionality conflicts.
items.unproven: generalizability of three scenarios to other development workflows; whether security-aware prompting degrades other model capabilities; durability under adversarial prompting

items.title: Practical Post-Quantum Cryptography for Bandwidth Constrained or Non-Terrestrial Networks, and Power Constrained Devices
items.dek: Shared secret keys replace post-quantum certificates to reduce bandwidth, memory, and energy costs for constrained networks and low-power devices.
items.unproven: key distribution and rotation mechanisms for adversarial environments; security proof against known attacks on pre-shared key schemes; scalability to device populations above thousands

items.title: SMARM+: Analyzing and Enhancing Shuffled Measurements for Remote Attestation in Real-Time IoT Settings
items.dek: SMARM remote attestation on real-time RTOS shows block size tightly couples attestation overhead to real-time availability; no tuning strategy overcomes both constraints.
items.unproven: whether proposed solutions in the truncated abstract actually resolve the block-size trade-off; tested on FreeRTOS and Zephyr only

items.title: Mission-Level Runtime Assurance for LLM-Assisted ISR Swarms over a Verification-Aware Fabric
items.dek: Three-tier runtime-verification framework for ISR swarms detects mission-level policy violations across agents; proof-of-concept on simulation, not production robotics.
items.unproven: deployment on real contested-environment swarms; verification fabric behavior under adversarial communication loss untested at scale

items.title: Rendering on Real Silicon: GPU Render-Timing as a Passive, AI-Resistant CAPTCHA Signal
items.dek: GPU render-timing under WebGL workload separates headless bots from real browsers by ~5x latency; resists AI automation.
items.unproven: Small labeled dataset (13 real GPUs); does not cover mobile/embedded GPUs, spoofing via custom render backends, or long-term evasion.

items.title: On AI Safety and Security Technical Debt in Engineering AI-Enabled Systems
items.dek: Taxonomy of 31 AI technical debt types across data, model, algorithm, and operations; organizes safety and security risks.
items.unproven: Systematic review of literature; does not provide measurement data, prioritization framework, or remediation roadmap for deployment decisions.

items.title: Tile's security is so bad it's a feature for stalkers
items.dek: Tile tracking device security weaknesses documented; hardware outside reader's SDLC scope.
items.unproven: scope limited to one product line; no implications for financial services software architecture

items.title: From Signals to Behaviors: Evidence-Based Android Malware Detection
items.dek: Praxis detects Android malware by recovering behaviors from static signals, confirming via code evidence, and judging in user and functional context.
items.unproven: evaluation against evolving malware families in the wild; false-positive rates on real app stores; scalability to current malware complexity

items.title: Accountable yet Anonymous AI Agents - Split-Knowledge Binding in National Agent-Identity Layer in China
items.dek: China's national AI-agent identity infrastructure uses split-knowledge binding to enable legal re-identification only via coordinated action by two separate agencies.
items.unproven: whether structural separation withstands determined state coercion; implementation details and failure modes; international applicability

items.title: Mask2Shield: Strengthening LLM Safety against Neuron-Pruning Attacks
items.dek: Mask2Shield reduces successful neuron-pruning attacks on LLM safety from 80–279 to 1–44 out of 313 prompts by training under masked-forward alignment.
items.unproven: whether defense generalizes to pruning methods not evaluated; capability preservation on safety-critical benchmark tasks; adaptive attacker with knowledge of defense

items.title: HiTMS: A High-Throughput Multi-Stream Linguistic Steganography Framework
items.dek: Multi-stream linguistic steganography framework batches secret embedding across LLM responses, achieving 4.3× throughput gain; theoretical capability without operational threat context.
items.unproven: real-world attack or defense scenario; frame design is novel but steganography via LLM sampling randomness remains a research construct

items.title: ATLAS: Automated Approximation of Transformers for Efficient Homomorphic Inference in One Hour
items.dek: Automated hyperparameter search reduces manual tuning for FHE transformer inference approximations.
items.unproven: Does not demonstrate production deployment or comparison against hand-tuned baselines in real inference workloads.

items.title: PATCH-FFT: Unmasking Dormant Hardware Trojans with Patch-Based Frequency-Domain Transformers
items.dek: Frequency-domain transformer detects dormant hardware Trojans in power traces at 90.94% accuracy.
items.unproven: Limited to simulation or lab silicon; does not demonstrate detection on real production hardware or integration into manufacturing test.

items.title: TroPUF: Evaluating Hardware Trojan Insertion in Delay-Based Physical Unclonable Functions
items.dek: Dormant Trojans embedded in delay PUFs evade conventional validation; modeling resistance persists until activation.
items.unproven: Framework tested on simulation; does not cover real fabricated silicon or cost of runtime detection overhead.

items.title: Early Detection of Hardware Trojans Using Neural Controlled Differential Equations and Analysis of Power Traces
items.dek: Neural Controlled Differential Equations on power traces detect dormant hardware Trojans above sensitivity threshold.
items.unproven: Validated on synthetic or limited benchmark data; does not establish detection reliability across process corners or production test integration.

items.title: Hiding in Plain Sight: An Effective Physical Adversarial Patch Attack against Visual-Infrared Fused Face Detection
items.dek: Physical adversarial patches evade visual-infrared face detection with over 90% success rate using gradient-color masks and stickers.
items.unproven: effectiveness against deployed fusion models in operationally realistic lighting and angle conditions; patch persistence under weathering

noise.title: Open-weight AI is having its Kubernetes moment
noise.dek: Essay comparing open-weight AI adoption to Kubernetes; no measurement or decision framework provided.
noise.unproven: no empirical data on security implications for agents entering SDLC

noise.title: Design is compromise
noise.dek: Essay on tradeoffs in design decisions and system constraints.
